full_judgment:
Fazle Munim, J.—While the Second Appeal No. 474 of 1972 is still pending for bearing under Order 41, rule 11, Civil Procedure Code both, the appellants and the plaintiffs-respondents No. 1 and 2 have filed this application for compromise. The question arises whether any order would be passed thereon as the appeal itself has not yet been admitted. 

 2. Mr. Latifur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the Plaintiffs Respondents Nos. 1 and 2.has cited a decision in the case of Mansur Mollah Vs. Shaikh Abdul Motaleb & anr., reported in 17 D.L.R Dacca 634, in support of the contention that this Court has power to pass such older. This decision is not to the point but states that an application for compromise may be filed not only in relation to a suit but to any proceeding. We are of the opinion that since the filing of the appeal, this Court would be in seisin of any matter therein, having the power to admit or dismiss it, it must also be said to have power to pass any order on such application as the present one, even though the appeal has not yet been admitted. 

 Heard the learned Advocates for the parties and perused the application for compromise, It is submitted by the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the appellant as well as the plaintiffs-respondents Nos. 1 and 2 who are parties to this compromise that the matters in dispute out of which this appeal has arisen have been settled between the parties who have joined in the compromise petition and it is prayed that the appeal be disposed of in terms of the compromise petition filed in Court today. We find that the terms of compromise as stated in paragraph 6 of the petition are lawful. 

 Let the appeal be allowed in terms of the compromise so far as the compromising parties are concerned; and the appeal as against the remaining respondents who have not joined in the compromise petition is hereby dismissed. The petition of compromise shall and do form part of the decree and the parties concerned do give effect to and be bound thereunder.
